articles.title: The People v. Gorilla Grodd Set Video Shows DC Villain Singing Backstreet Boys
articles.summary: The first glimpses of DC Studios’ The People v. Gorilla Grodd indicates it’s shaping up to be just as wacky as a TV show about a talking genius gorilla hailing from the creators of American Vandal could possibly get. The People v.
body: The People v. Gorilla Grodd is an eight-part true crime documentary series hosted by The Daily Planet’s Jimmy Olsen (once again played by Superman’s Skyler Gisondo ), who is investigating whether Grodd was wrongly imprisoned for killing his father, King Grodd.
Jimmy Tatro has been cast as Gorilla Grodd, but the actor recently explained that his role is mostly voice work and that motion-capture will be used to record his facial expressions.

That would explain why there’s a performer in a gorilla costume in the set photos and videos all over social media while the production films at Georgia Institute of Technology. It’s likely the suit performer is a stand-in for what will eventually become a CGI character.

The set photos and videos show Grodd attending Metropolis University, graduating in his cap and gown, singing with an a cappella group, and serenading a young woman with the Backstreet Boys’ "As Long as You Love Me". There are also videos showing what appears to be Tatro performing “Party Rock Anthem” (here’s another quick listen to Tatro’s voice as Grodd ).
points: The first glimpses of DC Studios’ The People v.
Gorilla Grodd indicates it’s shaping up to be just as wacky as a TV show about a talking genius gorilla hailing from the creators of American Vandal could possibly get.

articles.title: The Practical Acer 16" 1080p Portable USB Monitor Is on Sale For Just $39.99 at Best Buy
articles.summary: It's no surprise why USB portable monitors are so popular. They provide extra screen real estate for laptop users and they're much slimmer and lighter than your average monitor so you can carry them around.
body: Best Buy currently has the lowest price on a brand-name portable monitor. For a limited time, you can pick up a certified refurbished Acer 15.6" USB Portable Monitor (PM161Q) for just $39.99 with free shipping. It comes with a 90-day warranty.

The Acer PM161Q is a portable 15.6" monitor that weighs in at just 1.5 pounds and measures about 0.41" thin. It's small and slim enough to fit inside a laptop bag or backpack. It sports a sturdy metal frame and includes a cover that doubles as a kickstand. The 15.6" IPS display features a 1080p resolution (141ppi), 60Hz refresh rate, wide 178-degree viewing angle, and an anti-glare matte surface. It even has a built-in speaker.

Connectivity options include two USB Type-C ports and one mini HDMI port to connect to a laptop, tablet, or handheld gaming PC for use as a main or secondary display. If your device is equipped with a USB Type-C output with Power Delivery, then a single cable can be used for both video and power. Otherwise, you'll need two cables: a mini HDMI or USB Type-C cable for video and a second USB Type-C cable to a wall charger for power. All necessary cables are included.
points: It's no surprise why USB portable monitors are so popular.

articles.title: Investor Accidentally Pitches Kickass Pokemon Apocalypse Movie
articles.summary: For more than three decades, Pokemon and its various card and video games have enjoyed sustained popularity around the world. And at least one prominent collector and investor--Griffin Gaming Partners co-founder Peter Levin--believes that Pokemon's enduring appeal not only extends to the present…
body: "Pokemon is a global phenomenon," Levin told The Hollywood Reporter. "I'm absolutely convinced that if the world suffered an apocalypse tomorrow, the following day the global currency would be Pokemon cards. Pokemon cards are beating the S&P 500 by 3,000%. Emanating from Japan, it really took hold around the world in the late '90s and early 2000s. It then had a zenith moment and then a nadir moment, and ever since then, it's been on a parabolic growth curve."

As unlikely as that scenario might seem, there could be a very entertaining movie based on survivors using Pokemon cards as currency during an apocalypse. It would be probably even better with actual Pokemon--like the Detective Pikachu movie--but Levin's really hit on fun idea even if it doesn't have a basis in reality.

Everything Levin said about Pokemon's popularity is correct. There's a reason why the Japanese mob reportedly used rare Pokemon cards to launder money or for increasingly brazen robberies of Pokemon cards from stores across the US. Some people are willing to pay ridiculous amounts of money for the rarest Pokemon cards and collectibles.
points: For more than three decades, Pokemon and its various card and video games have enjoyed sustained popularity around the world.
"Pokemon is a global phenomenon," Levin told The Hollywood Reporter.
"I'm absolutely convinced that if the world suffered an apocalypse tomorrow, the following day the global currency would be Pokemon cards.
Pokemon cards are beating the S&P 500 by 3,000%.

articles.title: Valorant Cheater Using Evil Tung Tung Tung Sahur Skin Banned After Viral Video Sparks Backlash Against Riot's Anti-Cheat
articles.summary: A hacker using an ‘Evil’ Tung Tung Tung Sahur skin has been banned after wreaking havoc in Valorant lobbies and decimating entire teams. Cheaters are a never-ending issue in online multiplayer games, but some are more memorable than others.
body: Footage of the hacker went viral on social media, showing the cheater in third-person from what appears to be their own perspective. We can see the outlines of enemies through walls as Evil Tung walks backwards, shooting his gun at nothing — only for his opponents to drop like flies in a blink.

This video showed that the cheater seemed to have enabled wallhacks and auto-targeting, but it’s uncertain if they were using any other methods to decimate these lobbies. It took the Valorant community by storm, prompting popular analyst ‘vladk0r’ to post it as a jab against Riot's kernel-level anti-cheat system, Vanguard.

“Imagine losing to a team with this s**t only for them being banned later after [a] few rounds of the bracket, and not being able to do anything with this, ‘cause they got DQ’d much later after your match, so Riot can't revert the results,” he wrote.

“Proof that kernel-level anti-cheat compromises user privacy and security for nothing,” another player argued. “Cheaters own and control the hardware the game runs on, they always find a way eventually. You don't need more privilege in a client-side AC, you need server-side AC and behavioural analysis.”
points: A hacker using an ‘Evil’ Tung Tung Tung Sahur skin has been banned after wreaking havoc in Valorant lobbies and decimating entire teams.

articles.title: Nintendo Direct September 2026 No-Shows: From The Duskbloods to Mario
articles.summary: Today's September 2026 Nintendo Direct has come and gone, and so has any chance of seeing the next 3D Mario, The Duskbloods, and more highly anticipated games that ended up being no-shows.
body: Nintendo covered a lot in this morning's 45-minute slot. Metroid Ravenous is bringing Samus back for another 2D adventure, Kirby and the World Beyond is going 3D in 2027, and Mario Kart World is finally getting some much-needed love with a new update. Nintendo Switch 2 owners are eating well in more ways than one, but many fans say they were left starving for something a little more filling.

For instance, the company's hybrid sequel console is barreling through its second year without a proper 3D Mario to call its own. The Duskbloods, FromSoftware's vampire-themed Switch 2 exclusive multiplayer game, was nowhere to be seen despite still carrying a 2026 release window. Rumors suggesting new Super Smash Bros., Nintendogs, and Luigi's Mansion games were in the works really only helped build the mountain of no-shows overshadowing the show in fans' minds.

articles.title: A Full-Fledged Skyrim Mod Starring Matt Berry Is Here To Refresh The Game With An Ikea Ad
articles.summary: I am not enthusiastic about what feels like an inevitable future wherein games and gaming subscription services are inundated with advertisements. That said, I am excited to reinstall Skyrim so I can play an elaborate Ikea ad.
body: Newly released on Bethesda's Creations site, Kallax Storageborn is a remarkably in-depth Skyrim mod that features the titular Ikea item. But rather than simply adding the Kallax shelving unit as an item you can use to organize your in-game house, the mod turns it into a companion that follows you around, holding an unlimited number of items on your behalf. Oh, and the Kallax is voiced by Matt Berry.

You can get a taste of the mod in the video below, showing off Berry's performance and even a modified version of the opening "You're finally awake" sequence. There are new items to obtain, including the Allenblade, which looks like a giant allen wrench, and the Meatball Helmet.

With the mod installed, there's a new series of quests that kicks off to find the parts to assemble the Kallax, eventually all culminating in a boss fight. To trigger the quest, you'll have to become over-encumbered, which raises the need for a walking, talking shelving unit in the first place.
points: I am not enthusiastic about what feels like an inevitable future wherein games and gaming subscription services are inundated with advertisements.
That said, I am excited to reinstall Skyrim so I can play an elaborate Ikea ad.

articles.title: Gears Of War: E-Day Has A Smash Mouth-Inspired Achievement, And That’s Fantastic
articles.summary: Following the big Steam leak that revealed achievement lists and more for upcoming games, Microsoft has officially released the list of Achievements for Gears of War: E-Day, and there is a Shrek/Smash Mouth-inspired one among them.
body: Players can unlock an achievement called "HEY NOW, YOU'RE AN ALL STAR..." by accumulating 25,000 kills in the Versus multiplayer mode. This Achievement provides 25 Gamerscore.

The most difficult Achievement to unlock appears to be "Dead Serious," which requires players to 100% the campaign on the highest difficulty, Insane, reach 25,000 kills in Versus, achieve max player level, and max out four classes. Players who do that will be rewarded with 85 Gamerscore, which is the most for any single Achievement in the game.

It is a big year for both Xbox and Shrek, as both celebrate their 25th anniversaries this year. The original Shrek movie was re-released in theaters this past summer, and Shrek himself showed up in various video games. As for Xbox, the biggest news event for the 25th anniversary has been Microsoft's decision to lay off thousands of people, close development studios, and cancel games.

articles.title: Skyrim’s Wildest New Character Is a Talking Ikea Shelf, Voiced by Matt Berry
articles.summary: There are few things more humbling in The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim than finally defeating a powerful enemy, looting their corpse, and immediately discovering that you are carrying too much stuff to move. Thankfully, IKEA has arrived in Tamriel to solve Skyrim’s most persistent problem: clutter.
body: IKEA has released a new official Skyrim mod called Kallax Storageborn, a free mod that adds a sentient Kallax shelving unit as a companion. And because this is somehow a real thing that exists in 2026, the shelf is voiced by What We Do in the Shadows star Matt Berry.

The mod, which is available for free through Skyrim’s Creations system on Xbox and PC, kicks off when players become over-encumbered. From there, the Dragonborn is sent to an ancient dungeon and tasked with collecting the pieces needed to construct the mysterious Kallax. Once the shelf is assembled and equipped with a magical Allen wrench weapon, it comes to life and begins talking to the player in Berry’s unmistakable booming voice.

The mod also includes a full questline centered around Kallax and his mysterious past, with players helping the shelf recover heirlooms and memories. There are two IKEA-themed dungeons, a Clutter Golem boss fight, and new equipment including an Allen Key weapon and Meatball Helmet.

articles.title: We’ve Never Seen Anything Like This In Call Of Duty Before
articles.summary: Activision has revealed new information about one of the perks for preordering Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and it's a bit unusual. People who preorder the game on any platform get the Inner Circuit M4 weapon blueprint, but those who preorder on Xbox will get a translucent OG green version of…
body: If you preorder MW4 on any other platform, you'll get the same gun, but without the Xbox flourishes. Not only that, but if you're playing on PlayStation or Switch 2, you won't even see the translucent Xbox design. Only people playing on Xbox will.
Both versions of the gun are functionally identical, however, featuring the same attachments and gameplay characteristics.
Beyond this exclusive weapon variant, Microsoft is rewarding Xbox MW4 players by offering them a $5 credit to buy it on Xbox.

Microsoft owns Activision and the Call of Duty franchise, so this kind of exclusive offering makes sense. When Microsoft bought the franchise, it promised regulators that it would not water down Call of Duty games for platforms outside of Xbox, claiming 100% parity between platforms.

articles.title: Game of Thrones Is Officially Bringing Back Daenerys Targaryen
articles.summary: It's safe to say that Game of Thrones has become a cultural juggernaut. George R.R. Martin's book series, and the web of TV series that have been inspired by it, have been dominating our pop culture for years, and a few of the biggest characters are about to make a comeback.
body: Game of Thrones: War for Westeros, a new real-time strategy game from Playside Studios, premiered its latest trailer at Gamescom Opening Night Live last month. The trailer showcased the best look yet at the game's epic battles, all while confirming some of the characters who can lead a player's army. In addition to Jon Snow, Robb Stark, and Jaime Lannister, the trailer unveiled the game's take on two of the franchise's standout characters: Daenerys Targaryen (modeled after Emilia Clarke's portrayal on the TV show) and the Night King.

The trailer for War for Westeros also appeared to confirm that, once a player's army wins a match, their leader gets to sit on the Iron Throne. Depending on which character's army a player chooses, this might provide a sort of wish fulfillment, as the claim to the Iron Throne became very messy in the later seasons of the show. Daenerys, in particular, was just minutes away from claiming the Iron Throne when she was killed by Jon Snow... and her trusty dragon, Drogon, melted it after her death.
points: It's safe to say that Game of Thrones has become a cultural juggernaut.

articles.summary: The console war has found a new battlefield, and this time it’s the latest Call of Duty entry. Xbox players are getting a special Modern Warfare 4 gun skin that PlayStation and PC players literally cannot see.
body: Activision just announced the “Inner Circuit” M4 blueprint as a bonus for anyone who digitally pre-orders Modern Warfare 4.
While everyone gets the same weapon blueprint with identical stats, Xbox players get a very different-looking version.

The Xbox-exclusive treatment celebrates the console’s 25th anniversary with a translucent green design inspired by the original Xbox, complete with Xbox branding on the magazine. On Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Windows PC, the same weapon instead has a more traditional mil-spec appearance.
A console-exclusive skin on its own isn't odd, but here's where things get weird: The Xbox version isn't visible to anyone playing on another platform.

articles.title: After 43 years, Dragon Quest creator Yuji Horii is making a surprise sequel to his NES murder mystery game
articles.summary: This week's dual-pronged Nintendo Direct shows were stuffed with huge games. Kirby and the World Beyond! Metroid Ravenous! The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time! But the Japanese version of today's show quietly snuck in at least one game the rest of us didn't get: a sequel to Dragon Quest creator…
body: The Portopia Serial Murder Case came out a whopping 43 years ago - first on your personal computers, then on the NES - and the murder mystery romp went on to become a pretty big hit for Enix (now Square Enix ). Even Hideo Kojima once credited it as one of the reasons why he wanted to begin making games in the first place.

And in today's Nintendo Direct, we got a brand-new trailer for a sequel to The Portopia Serial Murder Case. The text-based detective work and witness interrogations from the original seem to be intact, alongside a new string of murders. Check it out below.

The Steam page also notes that Yuji Horii is supervising the project as an executive director, though there's sadly no sign of English-language support just yet. We should hear more as the game approaches its 2027 release window on Switch 2 and PC.

articles.title: Valheim 1.0's Steam player count soars to a huge 5-year high, but it's not enough to beat the viral survival game's early access peak
articles.summary: The five-year wait for Valheim 1.0 doesn't seem to have hurt the survival game behemoth's popularity all that much. After leaving early access, the crafty viking sim is enjoying a huge resurgence in Steam player numbers.
body: Still, Valheim hasn't been able to capture lightning in a bottle twice. At least, not yet. The game peaked over five years ago when 502,387 people logged on at the same time, aided by memes that sailed across the web and a playerbase that wasn't totally pandemic-free yet.

Today's Steam stats may also be skewed by the fact that Iron Gate's breakout game is now available to play on PS5, Nintendo Switch 2 and Xbox Series X/S consoles. The Valheim crowd on Steam no longer represents the entire Valheim crowd, then. We'll see how high those numbers soar as the game heads into its first proper weekend of release.

The Valheim 1.0 update arguably matches the game's incredible launch stats, too. Iron Gate's new patch notes are almost 1,800 words long and include too much new newness for me to neatly summarise here. Long story short, if you've not touched the procgen afterlife in a while, Valheim 1.0 adds a new biome called Deep North, over 40 fresh weapons, lots of new bits and bobs and hammers to craft, a graphics setting to stretch draw distances, and much more.
points: The five-year wait for Valheim 1.0 doesn't seem to have hurt the survival game behemoth's popularity all that much.

articles.title: How to mine the petrified Gammeltroll in Valheim
articles.summary: Have you met Valheim 1.0's mountainous menace, the Gammeltroll? If you've made your way to Valheim's final biome, the Deep North, you've probably seen and fought it already: the Gammeltroll is a 30-foot tall rock monster who pelts you with tree trunks from range and stomps you into paste if you get…
body: Most interestingly, when you defeat the Gammeltroll, it doesn't fall down. Instead, it turns into a statue called a "Petrified Gammeltroll." You can chip away at its legs all you want, but even the toughest pickaxe in the game won't make a dent. And as you might have guessed, inside the Gammeltroll awaits a critical new resource you'll need to conquer the frozen biome. So, how do you mine it?
The key to destroying the petrified Gammeltroll lies in the previous biome, the Ashlands, plus a new resource found in the Deep North.

Once you have ember charges, equip them and throw them at the petrified Gammeltroll. I find it best to throw them at its ankles from point blank range, then run away before they explode. With this method, it only takes two ember charges, one for each ankle, to destroy the statue.

When the troll collapses into a pile of rubble, collect your new resource, Petrified Tissue! Be warned, it's very heavy so you can't carry much, and it won't pass through wooden portals, only stone ones. Back at your base, throw it into your blast furnace and see what you get!
